dc: I will entrust my real sorrow to the heavenly Father, and receive in the waiting the peace he gives.

t: Sanctified by Truth, One in Christ
v: Sanctify them in your truth. Your word is truth.
As you sent me into the world, even so I have sent them into the world.
For their sakes I sanctify myself, that they themselves also may be sanctified in truth.
“Not for these only do I pray, but for those also who will believe in me through their word,
that they may all be one; even as you, Father, are in me, and I in you, that they also may be one in us; that the world may believe that you sent me.
The glory which you have given me, I have given to them, that they may be one, even as we are one,
I in them, and you in me, that they may be perfected into one, that the world may know that you sent me and loved them, even as you loved me.
Father, I desire that they also whom you have given me be with me where I am, that they may see my glory which you have given me, for you loved me before the foundation of the world.
Righteous Father, the world hasn’t known you, but I knew you; and these knew that you sent me.
I made known to them your name, and will make it known; that the love with which you loved me may be in them, and I in them.”
b: Before his suffering, Jesus asked the Father to sanctify the disciples in the truth, because the Father’s word is truth. He also sanctified himself for them, going toward the cross. Having been set apart, the disciples were still sent into the world. When God’s word exposes our prejudices, being willing to be reproved and to correct our conduct is a response to the Lord’s prayer.

Jesus’ prayer also included those who would later believe in him through the disciples’ word. He hoped they would all be one, so that the world would believe the Father had sent him. The church includes different generations and temperaments. When we disagree, we can listen in the truth, speak honestly, and admit our own faults, because we all belong to Jesus.

Jesus asked the Father that believers be with him, see his glory, and have the Father’s love in them. Christ binds us together. If someone in a small group is gradually going quiet, we can take the initiative to ask how he is doing, give him room to speak, and pray for trust to be restored between us. When the Lord’s love enters real relationships, the world can come to know, from how we live together, the Father who sent Jesus.
a: Let truth shed its light
Find one thing God’s word has already brought to my attention, and make one concrete correction today.
Take the initiative to build unity
Find a member who disagrees with me, first understand his situation, then say what I think.
Pray for those who do not yet believe
Ask God to let them see the gospel in believers’ love for one another.
q: In which relationship can I today obey the Lord’s word first and take a step toward unity?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, sanctify me in Your truth, and let me listen humbly even in disagreement and treat others according to Your word. May Jesus’ love dwell in us, so that people come to know You through the church’s unity. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ I pray, amen.
dc: I will obey God’s truth, and let Christ’s love make us one in him.

t: Cry Out from the Depths and Wait for God’s Salvation
v: Out of the depths I have cried to you, LORD.
Lord, hear my voice. Let your ears be attentive to the voice of my petitions.
If you, LORD, kept a record of sins, Lord, who could stand?
But there is forgiveness with you, therefore you are feared.
I wait for the LORD. My soul waits. I hope in his word.
My soul longs for the Lord more than watchmen long for the morning, more than watchmen for the morning.
Israel, hope in the LORD, for there is loving kindness with the LORD. Abundant redemption is with him.
He will redeem Israel from all their sins.
b: The psalmist cries to the LORD out of the depths. He does not say what trouble he has fallen into, but he asks a question that goes straight to the heart: if God marked iniquities, who could stand? This shows that when we cry out we may tell God our pain and also admit the wrongs we really have committed. With God there is forgiveness, so that the forgiven learn again to fear him and live frankly in his presence.

The watchman longs for morning in the deepest part of the night. The psalmist says he waits for the Lord more than watchmen wait for the morning. Because he has God’s word to hope in, he can keep opening his heart to God before circumstances change. While waiting there are still things we can do, such as admitting a wrong, mending a relationship, or letting brothers and sisters know we need prayer.

The psalm moves from one person’s cry to the hope of all Israel. Knowing that the LORD has loving kindness and plentiful redemption, the psalmist can say to those also in the dark that there is still reason to hope in God. Christ lets us see how this redemption comes to sinners. A person who has been forgiven can accompany another through a hard night, so that his cry is heard and they wait for the Lord together. At the next meeting, remember to ask about what was prayed for last time. Even when the situation has not changed for now, steady company lets the other know that someone is still willing to hope in the Lord with him.
a: Cry out honestly
Tell the Lord plainly what weighs on my heart most, and admit that I need his rescue.
Hope in God’s word
Keep a verse close at hand, and slow down to reread it when anxious.
Accompany one who is waiting
Contact a companion still in trouble, and ask what kind of support he needs most today.
q: When I feel I am in the depths, which word of God can hold me up as I wait for him?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, I cry to You from the depths of my heart. Thank You for hearing me and for being ready to forgive me. Help me hold fast to Your word as I wait, and let me accompany others who are waiting through the same night. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ I pray, amen.
dc: I hope in the God of loving kindness and plentiful redemption, and he hears my cry.

t: Be Strong and Courageous, Move Toward the Promise by God’s Strength
v: Now after the death of Moses the servant of the LORD, the LORD spoke to Joshua the son of Nun, Moses’ servant, saying,
“Moses my servant is dead. Now therefore arise, go across this Jordan, you and all these people, to the land which I am giving to them, even to the children of Israel.
I have given you every place that the sole of your foot will tread on, as I told Moses.
From the wilderness and this Lebanon even to the great river, the river Euphrates, all the land of the Hittites, and to the great sea toward the going down of the sun, shall be your border.
No man will be able to stand before you all the days of your life. As I was with Moses, so I will be with you. I will not fail you nor forsake you.
“Be strong and courageous; for you shall cause this people to inherit the land which I swore to their fathers to give them.

Only be strong and very courageous. Be careful to observe to do according to all the law which Moses my servant commanded you. Don’t turn from it to the right hand or to the left, that you may have good success wherever you go.

This book of the law shall not depart from your mouth, but you shall meditate on it day and night, that you may observe to do according to all that is written in it; for then you shall make your way prosperous, and then you shall have good success.
b: After Moses died, Joshua faced a new responsibility: leading the people across the Jordan. God did not ask him to retrace every step of his predecessor, but himself told him to arise, and promised to be with him as he had been with Moses. When we face a handover, a move, or a new trust, familiar support may be less. Joshua’s experience reminds us that God’s presence reaches across such changes.

God told Joshua several times to be strong and courageous, and once he tied it specifically to keeping the law. A leader most needs courage when everyone wants a shortcut and he knows he must hold to integrity. The courage of one at the head is first to let God’s word govern his direction. Even when he has the right to decide for himself, he is willing to stop and do as God commanded.

The book of the law was to be always on his lips, and he was to meditate on it day and night so that he would observe and do it. The prosperous way the text speaks of has to do with the mission God entrusted to Joshua. Today we can read Scripture into our daily work, letting it correct the tone of a meeting, the attitude toward people, and the reasons behind decisions. However large a new responsibility is, it still begins today with one decision that fits the Lord’s heart.
a: Say what I fear
Tell God plainly which part of the new responsibility makes me shrink back most.
Read Scripture for direction
Choose a verse from today, write it down, and name what it asks me to do.
Take one brave step
Complete one action I have put off out of fear but must now take on.
q: Facing a new trust, in which decision do I most need to rely on God to be strong today?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for being with me through changes. As I take on new responsibility, let me meditate on Your word day and night, give me courage to do it, and help me take today’s step with humility and faithfulness. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ I pray, amen.
dc: The faithful Lord is with me. I will take his word as my standard and go strongly toward what he has entrusted to me.

t: A Sinner Shown Mercy, Made a Vessel God Can Use
v: I thank him who enabled me, Christ Jesus our Lord, because he counted me faithful, appointing me to service,
although I used to be a blasphemer, a persecutor, and insolent. However, I obtained mercy because I did it ignorantly in unbelief.
The grace of our Lord abounded exceedingly with faith and love which is in Christ Jesus.
The saying is faithful and worthy of all acceptance, that Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners, of whom I am chief.
However, for this cause I obtained mercy, that in me first, Jesus Christ might display all his patience for an example of those who were going to believe in him for eternal life.
Now to the King eternal, immortal, invisible, to God who alone is wise, be honor and glory forever and ever. Amen.
b: Paul recalls that he had been a blasphemer, a persecutor, and an insolent man, and he admits these things frankly. He mentions that he acted ignorantly in unbelief, and he ascribes the mercy he received to the grace of Christ. Looking back, we can see where God stopped me and forgave me. Being able to name my wrongs and also count the grace I have received is a sign that one who has received grace is gradually maturing.

“Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners.” Paul calls himself the foremost of sinners because he knows from his own experience that the Lord can display patience toward one who once opposed him. Salvation turned him from persecutor to servant, and also gave those who later believed a visible example. When someone is afraid to come near the Lord because of what he did in the past, we can honestly share how Christ accepted us.

As soon as Paul mentions being appointed to service, he thinks of Christ who gave him strength, and finally offers praise to the King eternal. The experience, position, and results of ministry all give many reasons to thank God. When I receive a trust today, I can first ask the Lord for ability before starting, and after finishing tell how he upheld me through others. Serving this way lets those who hear the testimony also turn their eyes to the Lord.
a: Look back on the Lord’s mercy
Write down one specific past event in which I was forgiven and renewed.
Share my experience honestly
Tell someone who needs hope how patiently Jesus led me to turn back.
Answer a trust with thanks
After finishing an act of service, offer thanks to God, and thank those who took part.
q: Which part of my past can become a testimony that helps others know Christ’s mercy?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for forgiving me through Christ and for giving me the chance to serve. Help me remember how I received grace, and be willing to walk patiently beside those who are seeking You. May I be faithful in what I have received, and let all honor and glory be Yours. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ I pray, amen.
dc: I am a sinner who received mercy. I will serve faithfully in the strength Christ gives.

t: Hold Each Other Up and Go Farther Together
v: Two are better than one, because they have a good reward for their labor.
For if they fall, the one will lift up his fellow; but woe to him who is alone when he falls, and doesn’t have another to lift him up.
Again, if two lie together, then they have warmth; but how can one keep warm alone?
If a man prevails against one who is alone, two shall withstand him; and a threefold cord is not quickly broken.
b: The Preacher first speaks of a man alone, toiling and piling up wealth he cannot enjoy, and then says two are better than one. Two who labor together can share the results, and also have the chance to learn trust in living together. When we are so busy that only the to-do list remains, we easily forget those who walk with us. Setting aside a time to check in on one another may help us last longer than finishing one more task.

The Preacher uses three scenes, falling, cold, and attack, to show how practical company is. When a friend falls, a hand can lift him up. When a heart has gone cold, quietly sitting beside him may give him courage to speak again. To lift someone up, I can first ask which step is hardest for him, and then talk with him about how to share it. Admitting that I have fallen and being willing to receive help is also part of maturity.

A threefold cord is stronger than a single strand, because the strength is shared. A church small group can also cultivate this kind of trust. Starting with two companions praying for each other, we gradually learn to keep promises, speak honestly, and work together. When we disagree, we can read Scripture together and let Jesus govern our attitudes first. When people know that, in their weakness, someone is still willing to give them a hand, they can, once restored, go and help others. Support also needs steady habits. If we agree on which day to contact each other, we greet on time. If we promise to pray, we write down the other’s need. Real company is often built from many small acts of faithfulness.
a: Build a relationship of walking together
Arrange for a companion to share news, read Scripture, and pray for each other regularly, and set the next meeting time first.
Reach out in time
Care for someone in difficulty, and confirm one thing I can actually do.
Let others support me
Admit one burden to a trusted person and make one specific request.
q: In my life right now, which burden is suitable for a spiritual companion to carry with me?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for brothers and sisters who have walked with me through the ups and downs. Help me see who needs support, and give me humility to accept help. May Jesus be King in our relationships, so that we walk in Your way together. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ I pray, amen.
dc: I will receive the support the Lord gives through companions, and reach out a hand when others fall.

t: Fear God and Welcome the Sun of Righteousness
v: “For behold, the day comes, burning like a furnace, when all the proud and all who work wickedness will be stubble. The day that comes will burn them up,” says the LORD of Armies, “so that it will leave them neither root nor branch.
But to you who fear my name shall the sun of righteousness arise with healing in its wings. You will go out and leap like calves of the stall.
You shall tread down the wicked; for they will be ashes under the soles of your feet in the day that I make,” says the LORD of Armies.
“Remember the law of Moses my servant, which I commanded to him in Horeb for all Israel, even statutes and ordinances.
Behold, I will send you Elijah the prophet before the great and terrible day of the LORD comes.
He will turn the hearts of the fathers to the children and the hearts of the children to their fathers, lest I come and strike the earth with a curse.”
b: Malachi announces that the day of the LORD is coming. The proud and every evildoer will be like stubble, and will face God’s judgment. The previous chapter records that some, seeing evildoers apparently prosper, doubted what profit there was in serving God. The prophet turns people’s eyes to the justice God will one day make plain. When those who take shortcuts seem to gain, this promise gives those who fear God reason to keep walking in uprightness before him.

Those who fear God’s name will see the sun of righteousness rise, with healing in its wings. Their joy is like calves from the stall, finally free to leap about. A long injustice can make even hope feel like an effort. God knows the wounds people have suffered, and his justice brings the hope of healing. While waiting, people can seek appropriate help, and can also entrust the final judgment to God.

The passage ends by calling the people to remember the law of Moses, and foretells that Elijah will come to turn the hearts of fathers and children toward each other. The New Testament connects this to John the Baptist’s ministry of preparing the way of the Lord (Luke 1:16–17). Preparing to meet the Lord can begin with a strained relationship at home. We can admit the harsh words we have said, and at the right time sincerely care for one another.
a: Fear God in small things
Today, in one place where it is easy to conceal or cut corners, choose to act according to the truth.
Tell the Lord my pain
Pray over something long unresolved, and let a trusted person accompany me.
Turn my heart toward family
Pray over an estranged relationship, and at the right time take the initiative to listen.
q: Hoping for the Lord’s justice to be shown, how will that change how I treat those closest to me today?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, help me fear Your name and hold to integrity even when I see injustice. Heal the wounds in my heart, and give me courage to apologize for my own faults, so that my family’s hearts can again turn toward one another. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ I pray, amen.
dc: I fear God’s name and wait for him to show his justice. Today I will walk in his way.

t: Live Out Eternal Hope in Trials
v: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who according to his great mercy caused us to be born again to a living hope through the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead,
to an incorruptible and undefiled inheritance that doesn’t fade away, reserved in Heaven for you,
who by the power of God are guarded through faith for a salvation ready to be revealed in the last time.
In this you greatly rejoice, though now for a little while, if need be, you have been grieved in various trials,
that the proof of your faith, which is more precious than gold that perishes, even though it is tested by fire, may be found to result in praise, glory, and honor at the revelation of Jesus Christ—
whom, not having known, you love. In him, though now you don’t see him, yet believing, you rejoice greatly with joy that is unspeakable and full of glory,
receiving the result of your faith, the salvation of your souls.
b: Peter wrote to believers scattered in many places, and begins by praising God’s mercy. Through the resurrection of Jesus from the dead, God has given us new birth into a living hope. Peter points this hope to the inheritance kept in heaven for believers. When our resources, bodily strength, or familiar life change step by step, the risen Lord still holds our final destination and can be trusted.

Peter admits that believers are grieved by various trials, and says that faith that has been tested is more precious than gold. The picture of refining gold shows us that trials reveal whom the heart relies on. When caught in difficulty, I can first say honestly what I have lost, accept the support of companions, and ask the Lord to keep me doing what I should. These small acts of trust often prove especially real in hard days.

Though believers have not seen Jesus, they love him and believe in him, and rejoice with inexpressible joy because of salvation. This joy and tears can exist at the same time. When a person is still in trouble, hearing a verse or receiving a visit may help him remember again that the Lord loves him. The day Christ is revealed will let us see how precious in his eyes is the faithfulness that only God knows.
a: Say my sorrow aloud
Admit to the Lord the thing that has grieved me most lately, and ask a trusted person for help.
Remember the eternal destination
Reread today’s passage, and thank God for the inheritance he keeps.
Hold to faithfulness today
In a trial, choose one thing that fits the Lord’s heart and do it.
q: In the trial before me, how does the hope of resurrection hold me up as I keep trusting Christ?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for giving me a living hope through the risen Lord. Keep my faith in trials, let me dare to weep before You and be willing to accept the support of the body, and continue faithfully on the road before me. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ I pray, amen.
dc: Jesus has risen from the dead, and in trials I still have a living hope.

t: From Brokenness to Restoration, Living Out God’s Glory
v: The Lord GOD’s Spirit is on me, because the LORD has anointed me to preach good news to the humble. He has sent me to bind up the broken hearted, to proclaim liberty to the captives and release to those who are bound,
to proclaim the year of the LORD’s favor and the day of vengeance of our God, to comfort all who mourn,

to provide for those who mourn in Zion, to give to them a garland for ashes, the oil of joy for mourning, the garment of praise for the spirit of heaviness, that they may be called trees of righteousness, the planting of the LORD, that he may be glorified.
They will rebuild the old ruins. They will raise up the former devastated places. They will repair the ruined cities that have been devastated for many generations.
Strangers will stand and feed your flocks. Foreigners will work your fields and your vineyards.
But you will be called the LORD’s priests. Men will call you the servants of our God. You will eat the wealth of the nations. You will boast in their glory.
Instead of your shame you will have double. Instead of dishonor, they will rejoice in their portion. Therefore in their land they will possess double. Everlasting joy will be to them.
b: Isaiah describes an anointed one, on whom the Spirit of the Lord GOD rests, sent to bring good news to the humble, bind up the brokenhearted, and proclaim liberty to the captives. Jesus read this passage in Nazareth and declared it fulfilled in the hearing of his listeners (Luke 4:16–21). The brokenhearted often see only what they have lost. Jesus himself comes near them, so that they hear that God still remembers them.

A garland instead of ashes, the oil of gladness instead of mourning, describe the restoration God gives. Those who mourned in Zion will become oaks of righteousness, planted by the LORD, that he may be glorified. A tree takes time to grow, and a wounded life also needs company. Restoration can begin with naming the pain, slowly rebuilding trust, and then recovering strength to serve.

God also lets the comforted people rebuild the ruins. Restoration of a community includes repairing damaged homes, dignity, and life together. Today the church can work with a grieving person to discern what he most needs now, help him sort out his present life, and respect the pace of his recovery. The comfort he has received can later support others.
a: Entrust my wound to the Lord
Name one thing that still grieves me, and ask the Lord to comfort me in it.
Accompany a brokenhearted person
Listen first, then ask what time this week he needs someone to walk with him.
Take part in rebuilding
Mend a promise or a relationship, or help a family that needs support.
q: Which comfort God gave me can now become an act of accompanying someone else?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for coming near to the brokenhearted and oppressed through Jesus. Heal the wounds within me, and give me patience to walk with those who are recovering. May the rebuilding You do be a testimony among us, so that You are glorified. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ I pray, amen.
dc: I will receive the Lord’s comfort, and in him take part in mending wounded lives.

t: Lay Yourself Down and Live Out the Mind of Christ
v: If therefore there is any exhortation in Christ, if any consolation of love, if any fellowship of the Spirit, if any tender mercies and compassion,
make my joy full by being like-minded, having the same love, being of one accord, of one mind;
doing nothing through rivalry or through conceit, but in humility, each counting others better than himself;
each of you not just looking to his own things, but each of you also to the things of others.
Have this in your mind, which was also in Christ Jesus,
b: Paul first reminds the Philippian believers that in Christ they have already received encouragement and the comfort of love, and have fellowship in the Spirit. These graces are the starting point of being of one mind. When a church is divided in opinion, people easily remember only their own hurt. If we first recall together how the Lord accepted and comforted us, then before stating our own case clearly we can hear what the others have borne, leaving room in the relationship.

Paul points specifically to rivalry and vain conceit, because when a person is bent on proving himself, it is hard to look after others. He urges believers to have humility of mind, counting others better than themselves and looking to the interests of others. In a meeting, I can give the chance to speak to someone who has not yet spoken, and in a handover I can give a little more background so that the one taking over knows where things stand. These are visible forms of humility.

“Have this mind among yourselves, which is yours in Christ Jesus.” The verses that follow say that Christ willingly took the form of a servant, humbled himself, and was obedient even to death on a cross. Those who follow him can entrust reputation and credit to the Lord, and have strength left to notice others’ needs. When one on a team says, “This part was his contribution,” and another says, “This part I neglected,” trust between them has room to grow. Even when someone else’s proposal is the one finally adopted, we can still help as best we can and be glad for his growth. When after serving together everyone trusts one another more, Christ’s mind has already been seen in the team.
a: Recognize my own motives
Recall one quarrel, and ask what I most wanted to protect at that moment.
Practice listening first
Ask someone who disagrees to finish giving his reasons, and try to confirm what I heard in my own words.
Care for others’ difficulties
Today, in one shared responsibility, take the initiative to carry one task for a companion.
q: In a relationship now under strain, which thing would having the mind of Christ lead me to do first?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You that Jesus loved me with humility and obedience. Holy Spirit, show me my heart that seeks credit and clings to its own way, teach me to listen to others and admit my faults, and make me willing to take up my share of responsibility to serve people. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ I pray, amen.
dc: I will have the mind of Christ Jesus, and humbly look after those around me.

t: Affliction Turned Me Back, Truth Benefited Me
v: You have treated your servant well, according to your word, LORD.
Teach me good judgment and knowledge, for I believe in your commandments.
Before I was afflicted, I went astray; but now I observe your word.
You are good, and do good. Teach me your statutes.
The proud have smeared a lie upon me. With my whole heart, I will keep your precepts.
Their heart is as callous as the fat, but I delight in your law.
It is good for me that I have been afflicted, that I may learn your statutes.
The law of your mouth is better to me than thousands of pieces of gold and silver. YODH
b: The psalmist first admits that God has dealt well with him according to his word, and asks God to teach him good judgment and knowledge. Looking back, he says he went astray before he was afflicted, and now he is learning to keep God’s word. Looking back on a setback, we might ask what those days showed me and which one thing I can correct today. Examining ourselves honestly before God helps us return to the right path more than repeatedly blaming ourselves.

The psalmist was also attacked by the lies of the proud. He knew he had been wronged, yet he still sought God’s precepts with his whole heart. When we are misunderstood, we can state the facts clearly, seek suitable support, and ask the Lord to guard our words. Each time I want to strike back with a cutting remark, if I first stop and receive God’s guidance, truth can teach me honesty and restraint in the very place I was hurt. If I cannot think of a fitting thing to say for the moment, I can write down what happened, ask a mature companion to pray with me, and respond once I am sure what to say will help clear things up.

“It is good for me that I was afflicted, that I may learn your statutes.” This is the testimony the psalmist received from his own experience. In pain he came to know the worth of God’s word, even counting it better than thousands of gold and silver pieces. When life goes well, we can also store Scripture in our hearts ahead of time. When setbacks come, a word that we have thought over and practiced again and again can help us see how we can obey God in the moment.
a: Examine myself before God
Look back on a setback, and write down one thing I can correct today.
Answer misunderstanding with truth
State what happened as it was, and ask the Lord to keep me from hurtful replies.
Record the lesson learned
Write together one verse that helped me turn back and one action to put it into practice.
q: In what matter has my recent difficulty shown me I need God’s teaching more?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, You are good and do good. Be with me as I face pain, show me where I need to turn back, and teach me to keep Your word even when misunderstood. May I put the truth I have learned into practice in today’s life. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ I pray, amen.
dc: God’s word is more precious than gold and silver. I will be taught by him in difficulty and turn back to walk in his way.

t: The Savior Is Born, Glory to God
v: While they were there, the day had come for her to give birth.
She gave birth to her firstborn son. She wrapped him in bands of cloth and laid him in a feeding trough, because there was no room for them in the inn.
There were shepherds in the same country staying in the field, and keeping watch by night over their flock.
Behold, an angel of the Lord stood by them, and the glory of the Lord shone around them, and they were terrified.
The angel said to them, “Don’t be afraid, for behold, I bring you good news of great joy which will be to all the people.
For there is born to you today, in David’s city, a Savior, who is Christ the Lord.
This is the sign to you: you will find a baby wrapped in strips of cloth, lying in a feeding trough.”
Suddenly, there was with the angel a multitude of the heavenly army praising God and saying,
“Glory to God in the highest, on earth peace, good will toward men.”
When the angels went away from them into the sky, the shepherds said to one another, “Let’s go to Bethlehem, now, and see this thing that has happened, which the Lord has made known to us.”
They came with haste and found both Mary and Joseph, and the baby was lying in the feeding trough.
b: Luke records that Mary gave birth to her firstborn son, wrapped him in swaddling cloths, and laid him in a feeding trough. This baby whom the angel called Savior, Christ the Lord, was close to the life of ordinary people from his birth. When I feel I can offer only ordinary qualifications, the manger shows me that the Lord is willing to enter ordinary life, and can meet people in simple service.

The shepherds were keeping watch over their flock by night, and when the glory of the Lord shone around them they were terrified. The angel first said to them, “Don’t be afraid,” and then announced the good news of great joy. The good news of the Savior’s birth was first heard by people still working the night shift. In sharing the gospel we can learn this order: notice what the other person fears, and accompany him in hearing why Jesus came into the world.

The heavenly host praised God, giving glory to God in the highest, and proclaimed peace. The shepherds went to Bethlehem at once and saw the baby in the manger, just as they had been told. They answered the news they heard with action. Today we can begin with one relationship full of anxiety, pray about what worries us, and then, following his word, do one thing that brings peace. Thanks to the Savior then enters real life.
a: Remember the Savior’s birth
In a sentence of my own, thank God that Jesus came among us.
Notice people’s fears
Find someone under pressure lately, listen quietly, and pray for him.
Respond with action
According to the Lord’s word, complete one act of care, reconciliation, or service I have long wanted to do.
q: In the setting of daily life I know best, who needs to hear the good news that the Savior has come?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for giving the Savior Jesus. Help me notice his presence in ordinary life, and learn like him to draw near to those who are afraid. May I take obedient action with thanksgiving, and give the glory to You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ I pray, amen.
dc: The Savior Jesus has come. I will receive the peace he gives, and give glory to God.

t: Seek Jesus and Let the True King Reign
v: Now when Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judea in the days of King Herod, behold, wise men from the east came to Jerusalem, saying,
“Where is he who is born King of the Jews? For we saw his star in the east, and have come to worship him.”
When King Herod heard it, he was troubled, and all Jerusalem with him.
Gathering together all the chief priests and scribes of the people, he asked them where the Christ would be born.
They said to him, “In Bethlehem of Judea, for this is written through the prophet,
‘You Bethlehem, land of Judah, are in no way least among the princes of Judah; for out of you shall come a governor who shall shepherd my people, Israel.’”
He sent them to Bethlehem, and said, “Go and search diligently for the young child. When you have found him, bring me word, so that I also may come and worship him.”
They, having heard the king, went their way; and behold, the star, which they saw in the east, went before them until it came and stood over where the young child was.
When they saw the star, they rejoiced with exceedingly great joy.
They came into the house and saw the young child with Mary, his mother, and they fell down and worshiped him. Opening their treasures, they offered to him gifts: gold, frankincense, and myrrh.
Being warned in a dream not to return to Herod, they went back to their own country another way.
b: Wise men from the east came to Jerusalem and asked where the one born King of the Jews was. They had traveled far to seek a king. Herod was troubled when he heard it, and gathered the chief priests and scribes to inquire. They pointed to Bethlehem. After understanding a passage, we can go on to ask how far I am willing to go in the truth I have understood.

Herod asked the wise men to search out news of the child, saying he wanted to go and worship him as well. When the wise men came before Jesus, they bowed down and worshiped, and opened their treasures to offer gifts. True worship touches what we value most. Letting Jesus be King means being willing to let him decide how time is used and how interests are arranged, and letting him deal with the power I grip tightly.

The wise men were warned in a dream and returned home by another way. After meeting Jesus, their journey really did change. After worshiping today, we too can change one way of doing things or take back one harsh word. Following the direction Scripture points, asking the Holy Spirit to lead me to do it, brings worship back into ordinary life.
a: Let Scripture point the way
From what I read today, find one thing I can put into practice.
Hand a decision to the Lord
Pray over the one thing I most want to control, and rearrange it according to the Lord’s heart.
Worship with action
Use some time or a resource to help someone in need, and offer thanks to the Lord.
q: Which long-held decision that I have gripped myself do I want to hand over to Jesus?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for leading me to seek Jesus. Help me seek the Lord and worship him, and be willing to let him govern my decisions. Give me courage to do what Your word says. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ I pray, amen.
dc: Jesus is my King. I will offer him what I treasure, and do what his word says.

t: Fan the Gift into Flame, Live Out the Gospel with Strength
v: I thank God, whom I serve as my forefathers did, with a pure conscience. How unceasing is my memory of you in my petitions, night and day
longing to see you, remembering your tears, that I may be filled with joy;
having been reminded of the sincere faith that is in you, which lived first in your grandmother Lois and your mother Eunice and, I am persuaded, in you also.
For this cause, I remind you that you should stir up the gift of God which is in you through the laying on of my hands.
For God didn’t give us a spirit of fear, but of power, love, and self-control.
Therefore don’t be ashamed of the testimony of our Lord, nor of me his prisoner; but endure hardship for the Good News according to the power of God,
who saved us and called us with a holy calling, not according to our works, but according to his own purpose and grace, which was given to us in Christ Jesus before times eternal,
but has now been revealed by the appearing of our Savior, Christ Jesus, who abolished death, and brought life and immortality to light through the Good News.
Hold the pattern of sound words which you have heard from me, in faith and love which is in Christ Jesus.
That good thing which was committed to you, guard through the Holy Spirit who dwells in us.
b: Paul remembers Timothy’s tears, and remembers the faith of his grandmother Lois and his mother Eunice. Timothy had received the nurture of those before him and had also received God’s gift. Paul urges him to fan the gift into flame. When service has worn us out, we can accept company, and then begin practicing again from what is within our ability.

God has given a spirit of power, love, and self-control. Power lets a person acknowledge that he belongs to the Lord, love lets him consider those who hear, and self-control lets him be sober and restrained. Paul mentions that he is in prison, and encourages Timothy to share in suffering for the gospel by the power of God. Christ has already shed light on life through the gospel, which gives us hope even in the face of cost.

Paul charges Timothy to hold the pattern of sound words, and by the Holy Spirit who dwells in us to guard the good deposit entrusted to him. In using our gifts, we can let Scripture correct the content, let the Holy Spirit guide the attitude, and let trusted companions give feedback. Let us pass the truth we have received on to the next person honestly and gently.
a: Restore one practice
This week, find an occasion to use again one gift the Lord has given me.
Speak up for the gospel
At a fitting moment, say briefly how Jesus has helped me, and listen to the other’s response.
Faithfully guard what is entrusted
When preparing to share, first read the passage’s context clearly, and ask a companion for feedback.
q: Which gift that I have set aside out of tiredness or fear can I practice again today, relying on the Lord?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for nurturing me through others and for giving me gifts for service. Holy Spirit, give me a spirit of power, love, and self-control, so that I stay faithful to the gospel You have entrusted and serve people with the strength You give. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ I pray, amen.
dc: By the Holy Spirit within me I will fan my gift into flame, and witness to the gospel with strength and love.

t: Let Christ Dwell in Your Heart and Live Out Boundless Love
v: that he would grant you, according to the riches of his glory, that you may be strengthened with power through his Spirit in the inner person,
that Christ may dwell in your hearts through faith, to the end that you, being rooted and grounded in love,
may be strengthened to comprehend with all the saints what is the width and length and height and depth,
and to know Christ’s love which surpasses knowledge, that you may be filled with all the fullness of God.
b: Paul prays for the Ephesian believers, asking the Father, according to the riches of his glory, to strengthen them with power through his Spirit in the inner being. Even when outward things cannot be changed for now, God can still support a person’s heart and give him strength to trust. When a relationship hits a deadlock, or responsibility wears us out, we can first admit our limits to the Father and ask him to add strength within us, so that we have courage to face the people and matters in front of us.

Christ dwells in our hearts through faith, so that our love is rooted and grounded. Only roots that go deep can bear the changing seasons, and only a house with a firm foundation can stand against the wind. If a person has strength to love only when affirmed, his love will rise and fall with the other’s response. Each time we return to the gospel and recall how Jesus accepted me even when I failed, I can more freely apologize and listen, and within proper boundaries give the other person practical care.

Paul hopes believers will “together with all the saints” grasp Christ’s love, and says this love surpasses knowledge. The breadth and length and height and depth of love are often gradually known through the company of the members of the church. Someone who still visits when I have no strength, someone who still honestly reminds me when I am wrong: these experiences teach me how to accompany the next person. As mutual trust grows deeper, we are also better able to receive the fullness of God, letting his love reach places we were unwilling to open. When I meet someone hard to get along with, I can first pray for him, and then ask which action would both look after his needs and protect our trust in each other.
a: Ask the Lord to strengthen my heart
At the start of the day, pray to the Father about a relationship that wears me out.
Remember that the Lord loved me first
Recall one time Christ accepted me, and offer him thanks.
Learn to love with companions
This week invite a brother or sister to share an experience of being loved, and choose one concrete act to care for him.
q: In which relationship can I, because I am already loved by Christ, take a step of loving?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, strengthen my heart through Your Spirit, and let Christ dwell in my heart through faith. May I be rooted in his love, and together with all the saints receive the love that surpasses knowledge, and turn it into patience and practical care for those around me. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ I pray, amen.
dc: Christ dwells in my heart through faith. I will be rooted in his love, and live out this love together with all the saints.

t: Immanuel, God with Us
v: Now the birth of Jesus Christ was like this: After his mother, Mary, was engaged to Joseph, before they came together, she was found pregnant by the Holy Spirit.
Joseph, her husband, being a righteous man, and not willing to make her a public example, intended to put her away secretly.

But when he thought about these things, behold, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream, saying, “Joseph, son of David, don’t be afraid to take to yourself Mary as your wife, for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Spirit.
She shall give birth to a son. You shall name him Jesus, for it is he who shall save his people from their sins.”
Now all this has happened that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the Lord through the prophet, saying,
“Behold, the virgin shall be with child, and shall give birth to a son. They shall call his name Immanuel,” which is, being interpreted, “God with us.”
Joseph arose from his sleep, and did as the angel of the Lord commanded him, and took his wife to himself;
and didn’t know her sexually until she had given birth to her firstborn son. He named him Jesus.
b: When Mary became pregnant by the Holy Spirit, what Joseph knew was still very limited. He was a righteous man, and meant to divorce her quietly so as not to put her to shame in public. When God guided him through an angel in a dream, he was willing to revise his plans according to what he had received. When we meet something hard to understand, we too can first protect people’s dignity, find out what happened according to the truth, and only then make the decisions that require us to bear responsibility.

The angel told Joseph to name the child Jesus, because he would save his people from their sins. People sometimes ask God to make things go smoothly, and Jesus also comes to save us from the grip of sin. When a lie could get me out of trouble for the moment, or an act of revenge could feel satisfying, I can ask him for help and make the harder choice that fits the truth.

Matthew quotes the prophet, pointing out that this child is “Immanuel,” which means God with us. When Joseph woke, he did as he was told and took Mary as his wife, and later named the child Jesus. Believing that God was with him became, for him, a series of concrete actions. Today, the Lord’s presence can also help us faithfully take on the responsibility we already understand, even while circumstances are still difficult.
a: Protect people’s dignity
Before finding out what happened, first guard my own words.
Ask the Savior for help
Honestly admit one sin that keeps trapping me, and ask the Lord to lead me to change.
Obey in his presence
Pray over a responsibility that is hard to face, and today do the step I am able to do.
q: Believing God is with me, how would I take on today a responsibility I would rather push away?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for giving Jesus, who saves me from sin and is himself with me. Teach me to seek patiently when I do not understand, to obey bravely once I understand Your will, and to treat those around me with love and honesty. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ I pray, amen.
dc: God is with me. By the Savior Jesus I will faithfully take on today’s trust.

t: Hear the Gospel, Experience Jesus, Proclaim Salvation
v: When the angels went away from them into the sky, the shepherds said to one another, “Let’s go to Bethlehem, now, and see this thing that has happened, which the Lord has made known to us.”
They came with haste and found both Mary and Joseph, and the baby was lying in the feeding trough.
When they saw it, they publicized widely the saying which was spoken to them about this child.
All who heard it wondered at the things which were spoken to them by the shepherds.
But Mary kept all these sayings, pondering them in her heart.
The shepherds returned, glorifying and praising God for all the things that they had heard and seen, just as it was told them.
b: After the angels left, the shepherds said to one another that they would go to Bethlehem and see the thing the Lord had made known. They went with haste, and found Mary, Joseph, and the baby lying in the feeding trough. The gospel is first heard with the ears, and then can enter people’s lives. When the Lord’s word prompts us to take initiative in caring, repenting, or forgiving, we can first do one small act and experience his leading for ourselves.

After the shepherds saw it, they spread the word that had been told them about this child. They could say plainly what they had heard in the night and what they had seen in Bethlehem. Sharing a testimony can likewise begin with concrete facts. Telling how I met Jesus and how I have changed because of him, and leaving time for questions, often helps the other person understand how the gospel relates to his own life.

All who heard it wondered, Mary kept these things in her heart and pondered them, and the shepherds returned, glorifying and praising God. These responses bring us to two everyday things: quietly remembering the Lord, and thanking him in our original life. Returning to work and family, we can keep a passage in mind, review how it has changed the decisions I make, and prepare to share it at a fitting time. After sharing, we can still care for the other person, ask what he most wants to understand, and arrange a time to read a short section of a Gospel together.
a: Respond promptly to what I have heard
Pick one reminder I can carry out today, pray quietly, and then go and do it.
Prepare a short testimony
Write down how things were before, how I met the Lord, and one change I see now.
Give thanks in daily life
Tonight, recall one time I was led by the Lord at work or at home, and offer God praise.
q: Which recent experience of the Lord’s leading can I share in my own words with relatives and friends?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for letting me hear the gospel of the Savior. Make me willing to act like the shepherds, and able, like Mary, to keep Your works in my heart. May I remember You in familiar life and share my own experience at a suitable time. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ I pray, amen.
dc: I will respond to the gospel I have heard, tell of the Lord’s works, and give glory to God.

t: Understand God’s Word and Receive the Strength of Joy
v: Ezra the priest brought the law before the assembly, both men and women, and all who could hear with understanding, on the first day of the seventh month.

He read from it before the wide place that was in front of the water gate from early morning until midday, in the presence of the men and the women, and of those who could understand. The ears of all the people were attentive to the book of the law.

Ezra the scribe stood on a pulpit of wood, which they had made for the purpose; and beside him stood Mattithiah, Shema, Anaiah, Uriah, Hilkiah, and Maaseiah, on his right hand; and on his left hand, Pedaiah, Mishael, Malchijah, Hashum, Hashbaddanah, Zechariah, and Meshullam.
Then Ezra blessed the LORD, the great God. All the people answered, “Amen, Amen,” with the lifting up of their hands. They bowed their heads, and worshiped the LORD with their faces to the ground.
They read in the book, in the law of God, distinctly; and they gave the sense, so that they understood the reading.

Nehemiah, who was the governor, Ezra the priest and scribe, and the Levites who taught the people said to all the people, “Today is holy to the LORD your God. Don’t mourn, nor weep.” For all the people wept when they heard the words of the law.

Then he said to them, “Go your way. Eat the fat, drink the sweet, and send portions to him for whom nothing is prepared, for today is holy to our Lord. Don’t be grieved, for the joy of the LORD is your strength.”
b: After the wall of Jerusalem was rebuilt, the people gathered in front of the Water Gate and asked Ezra to bring the book of the law of Moses. Those who could understand listened from early morning until midday. The wall was finished, but the people still needed to reorder their lives through God’s word. After completing a great task, we also need to hear God’s word afresh.

Ezra blessed the LORD, and the people lifted up their hands in response and bowed down in worship. The Levites read the book of the law of God distinctly, gave the sense, and caused the people to understand the reading. When leading a small group in reading Scripture, we can read clearly, explain to whom the text was addressed and in what setting, and then ask everyone to say in their own words what they understood.

The people wept as they heard the law, and the leaders reminded them that the day was holy, a day to eat and drink and also to send portions to those who had nothing prepared. Joy from the LORD gives people strength to care for those in need. When God’s word has shone on us, we can confess our sins, and also rejoice that he still invites me to return.
a: Set aside time to listen attentively
Read a passage, and write down what it meant in its original setting.
Put into practice what I understand
Choose one truth, and share in the small group how we can do it today.
Share with those in need
Use a meal, supplies, or some time to let someone taste the Lord’s grace.
q: Which word of God I have understood recently can become an action that brings joy to others too?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for teaching us by Your word. Give me a heart that listens attentively, so that once I understand I do it, and in repentance receive Your joy, and gladly share the grace I have received with those in need. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ I pray, amen.
dc: I will listen attentively and understand God’s word, find joy and strength in him, and share his grace with others.

t: Though Your Soul Is Downcast, Still Hope in God
v: As the deer pants for the water brooks, so my soul pants after you, God.
My soul thirsts for God, for the living God. When shall I come and appear before God?
My tears have been my food day and night, while they continually ask me, “Where is your God?”
These things I remember, and pour out my soul within me, how I used to go with the crowd, and led them to God’s house, with the voice of joy and praise, a multitude keeping a holy day.
Why are you in despair, my soul? Why are you disturbed within me? Hope in God! For I shall still praise him for the saving help of his presence.
b: The psalmist likens his longing for the living God to a deer panting for streams of water. A deer needs water to live, and the psalmist also longs to see God again. He has made tears his food day and night, while others keep asking him, “Where is your God?” In sorrow a person especially needs God, and may find it especially hard to feel his presence. This psalm lets us know that praying to God with questions and tears is itself a kind of longing.

The psalmist remembers leading the multitude to the house of God in the past, shouting and praising among the crowd at the feast. Good memories made his soul feel poured out, and also reminded him that he had personally known joy in worship with others. For someone who has been away from a familiar community for a time, a gentle greeting, or taking part in a gathering again when he can bear it, may help him through lonely days.

He asks his soul why it is downcast, and urges himself to hope in God, for he will yet praise him. This is a true word that one who weeps says to himself. When our mood cannot change for the moment, we can still pray, speak to God with the Psalms, and ask trusted people to be with us. If we can sing one line, sing one line; if we can walk one step, walk one step, letting hope slowly grow back in the company of God and the body of believers. To accompany someone who is downcast, we can also agree on the next time to meet. When someone is willing to keep listening to him, it helps him remember through long days that he has someone walking with him.
a: Let tears enter prayer
Read the psalmist’s words quietly, then say my own heaviness in my own words.
Recall a time of grace
Write down one memory of being comforted in worship or in walking with others.
Accept some company
Contact a trusted member, and arrange a time to walk, talk, or pray together.
q: When my soul is downcast, how can I keep hoping in God within my real feelings?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, You know the thirst in my heart and have seen the tears I have shed. Let me come honestly before You, remind my heart with Your word, and accept the company You give through brothers and sisters. May I still hope in You in dark days. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ I pray, amen.
dc: My soul longs for the living God. Even if I am still downcast, I will hope in him.

t: Live as a Child of God and Become Like Christ
v: See how great a love the Father has given to us, that we should be called children of God! For this cause the world doesn’t know us, because it didn’t know him.
Beloved, now we are children of God. It is not yet revealed what we will be; but we know that when he is revealed, we will be like him, for we will see him just as he is.
Everyone who has this hope set on him purifies himself, even as he is pure.
Everyone who sins also commits lawlessness. Sin is lawlessness.
You know that he was revealed to take away our sins, and no sin is in him.
Whoever remains in him doesn’t sin. Whoever sins hasn’t seen him and doesn’t know him.
Little children, let no one lead you astray. He who does righteousness is righteous, even as he is righteous.
He who sins is of the devil, for the devil has been sinning from the beginning. To this end the Son of God was revealed: that he might destroy the works of the devil.
Whoever is born of God doesn’t commit sin, because his seed remains in him, and he can’t sin, because he is born of God.
b: John invites believers to see what kind of love the Father has given us, that we should be called children of God. He adds that we are God’s children now, and it has not yet been revealed what we will be, but when he appears we will be like him. Identity comes before growth. When we once more see our weakness, we can return to the Father because of his love, and because of the hope of being like the Lord, be willing to purify today’s life.

Jesus appeared to take away sins, and in him is no sin. John uses strong words to point out that for those who abide in Christ, life changes direction. Earlier in this letter he also teaches believers to confess their sins, and points to the advocate who speaks for us (1 John 1:9, 2:1). When we fall, we can come back to the Lord frankly, admit what we did, and seriously deal with the habits that easily make us repeat it.

The Son of God appeared to destroy the works of the devil. The new life from God grows in believers and gradually bears the fruit of righteous actions. If in the past I was used to covering up mistakes, today I can tell the truth. If I was used to using my position to press people down, today I can really listen to others. When we let Jesus be King in one concrete choice, we begin to live out in action the identity the Father has given.
a: Remember my identity as a child
In my own words, thank the heavenly Father for accepting me as his child.
Confess my sins to the Lord
Name the sin I most often repeat, and ask a trusted companion to watch over me.
Live out righteousness in action
In a matter where I could cover up or shift blame, honestly take my share of responsibility.
q: Knowing I am a beloved child of God, in what matter will I be more willing to be like Jesus today?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for calling me Your child. Help me return to You frankly when I fall, to turn from sin through Jesus, and to gradually take on his likeness in today’s words and actions. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ I pray, amen.
dc: I am a beloved child of the heavenly Father. I will abide in Christ and live out his likeness every day.

t: Be Alert in Disaster and Turn Back to God
v: The LORD’s word that came to Joel, the son of Pethuel.
Hear this, you elders, and listen, all you inhabitants of the land! Has this ever happened in your days, or in the days of your fathers?
Tell your children about it, and have your children tell their children, and their children, another generation.
For a nation has come up on my land, strong, and without number. His teeth are the teeth of a lion, and he has the fangs of a lioness.
He has laid my vine waste, and stripped my fig tree. He has stripped its bark, and thrown it away. Its branches are made white.
Mourn like a virgin dressed in sackcloth for the husband of her youth!
The meal offering and the drink offering are cut off from the LORD’s house. The priests, the LORD’s ministers, mourn.
The field is laid waste. The land mourns, for the grain is destroyed, The new wine has dried up, and the oil languishes.
Be confounded, you farmers! Wail, you vineyard keepers, for the wheat and for the barley; for the harvest of the field has perished.

The vine has dried up, and the fig tree withered— the pomegranate tree, the palm tree also, and the apple tree, even all of the trees of the field are withered; for joy has withered away from the sons of men.
b: The word of the LORD came to Joel, first telling the elders and all the inhabitants of the land to listen carefully, and to tell their children and grandchildren of the disaster they had lived through. The vines, the fig trees, and the fields were laid waste one after another, and the harvest people lived on was destroyed. The prophet invites all the people to face the facts together. When a great loss comes, the church can also accompany those affected as they face the facts and sort out their present life.

The passage calls the people to wail, like a virgin dressed in sackcloth for the husband of her youth. The fields are ruined, and the meal offering and the drink offering are cut off from the house of the LORD. The disaster affects livelihood and worship, and grief needs someone to share it. When listening to someone speak of what he has lost, we can also ask whether he needs food, transportation, or company.

Joel then calls people to fast, to gather, and to cry out before God (Joel 1:13–14). A crisis can make us stop and examine what we usually rely on, and honestly turn back when God points out sin. Accompanying those struck by disaster begins with weeping with them and with aid. We can pray to God while setting aside indifference, and care for those around us with whatever resources are in our hands.
a: Face the loss honestly
Tell God about the difficulty, and let a trusted companion know what I need.
Examine myself before God
Ask him to show me one responsibility I usually neglect, and take action today.
Care for those who suffer
Choose one concrete form of help, and reach out according to the other person’s actual need.
q: Facing the difficulty before me, in what matter will I turn back to God, and respond to people’s needs with action?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, keep me alert in difficulty, let me see my own responsibility clearly, and hear the voice of those who suffer. May I turn to You honestly, pray with my brothers and sisters, and support those in need with practical action. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ I pray, amen.
dc: I will turn to God in difficulty, cry out together with those who suffer, and reach out to support one another.

t: God’s Promise Is an Anchor for the Soul
v: For when God made a promise to Abraham, since he could swear by no one greater, he swore by himself,
saying, “Surely blessing I will bless you, and multiplying I will multiply you.”
Thus, having patiently endured, he obtained the promise.
For men indeed swear by a greater one, and in every dispute of theirs the oath is final for confirmation.
In this way God, being determined to show more abundantly to the heirs of the promise the immutability of his counsel, interposed with an oath,
that by two immutable things, in which it is impossible for God to lie, we may have a strong encouragement, who have fled for refuge to take hold of the hope set before us.
This hope we have as an anchor of the soul, a hope both sure and steadfast and entering into that which is within the veil,
where as a forerunner Jesus entered for us, having become a high priest forever after the order of Melchizedek.
b: When God made his promise to Abraham, since he could swear by no one greater, he swore by himself. After patient endurance, Abraham obtained what God promised. Through his experience Hebrews reminds those who inherit the promise that God’s purpose is dependable, and that his promise and oath give us strong encouragement. When the wait grows long, we can think again about what truly comes from God, and trust his faithfulness alone.

The author likens the hope we hold to an anchor of the soul, sure and steadfast, and entering into the inner place behind the veil. A ship is still tossed in wind and waves, but with an anchor there is something to hold it steady. The place where this hope is fixed is God’s presence. When people’s opinions and circumstances keep shifting, we can follow this line back to the Lord, pray, hear his word, and do what we already know we should do today.

Jesus has gone as forerunner on our behalf into the inner place behind the veil, having become a high priest forever after the order of Melchizedek. “Forerunner” shows us that he walks ahead of us and has opened the way for us to draw near to God. When we feel uneasy about tomorrow, we can draw near to the Father today, tell him our deepest worries in his presence, and hold on to hope together with companions. Jesus before the Father is enough to hold up our faith.
a: Reread God’s promise
Write down one sentence from Scripture about God’s faithfulness, and put it where I can see it when anxious.
Bring worry into prayer
Tell the heavenly Father about one matter still waiting, and entrust the timing and outcome to him.
Help someone hold on to hope
Care for a companion who is waiting, and pray for what each of us can do today.
q: In the matter that feels most unsteady right now, how can my heart fix its hope on Jesus, who has entered behind the veil?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You that Your promise is faithful and sure, and thank You that Jesus has opened the way for us to draw near to You. Steady my heart in the waiting, so that I hold fast to the hope in Christ and faithfully take today’s step. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ I pray, amen.
dc: God’s promise is the sure anchor of my soul. By Jesus I will hold fast to hope.
